messages:
Aisha Khan: quick sync — we need to pick the top 3 observability pieces for Q2 launch. customers driving this: ACME (per-route costing + trace links), Nimbus (error spike dashboards), and several smaller SaaS customers asking for sampling controls. i sketched a strawman below.
Jo Park: show the strawman pls — we should be explicit about launch criteria (GA vs beta) and what 'shippable' means.
Aisha Khan: strawman: 1) per-route/token cost breakdown in console (GA), 2) tracing hook: UI link to traces + lightweight sampling toggle (beta->GA), 3) error analytics: grouped stack traces + alerting rules (beta).
Carlos Mendes: +1 on ordering. note runtime concerns: per-route costing needs token attribution from the routing layer — requires a small telemetry envelope change.
Maya Liu: infra note — attribution change is low perf risk but needs DB schema for aggregation (hourly route counters). ETA ~3 sprints for safe rollout unless we accept a simpler initial surface (per-model only).
Sam O'Neil: frontend: per-route breakdown table + sparkline is quick. metric names: route_id, model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd. sample UI stub: ```json
{"columns":["route","tokens","cost","95p_latency"]}
```
Jo Park: launch criteria proposal: GA for per-route cost = (1) accurate-to-within-5% on canonical workloads, (2) trailing 7-day sampling enabled by default, (3) rollout flag and rollbacks tested. tracing hook GA = link to trace explorer + sampling control; error analytics GA = grouping + one alert template.
Carlos Mendes: prioritization tradeoff: if we only do per-model aggregation we can ship cost surface in 2 sprints and pair with a roadmap note to expand to per-route. customers like ACME will push back though.
Aisha Khan: decision needed: ship per-model fast or delay for per-route? we could ship per-model with a clear migration path and a "per-route coming soon" banner. Thoughts?
Maya Liu: prefer incremental. per-model first, but add telemetry that records route->model mapping so we don't need a heavy migration later.
Sam O'Neil: agree. UI will render both modes if mapping exists. if not, show "route mapping missing" CTA to docs.
Jo Park: risks: billing clarity for enterprise contracts — finance needs exactness. add requirement: finance sign-off for any GA that affects invoices.
Carlos Mendes: noted. also: tracing hook sampling toggle defaults to "adaptive" to avoid cost spikes. we should include a simple CLI toggle for customers: `redwood obs sampling set --route R --rate 0.01`
Aisha Khan: good. rollout plan: week 1 internal dogfood (10% traffic), week 2 invited customers (20%), week 3 general availability. success metrics: <5% unexpected cost variance, no regression in 95p latency, adoption by 3 pilot customers.
Sam O'Neil: can we ship with 7-day retention to start? more retention is expensive.
Maya Liu: yes — start with 7-day, have premium tier for 90-day export. note: backups for legal/enterprise may need longer retention API.
Jo Park: action items: 1) Aisha: get finance sign-off on billing wording by EOD Thurs. 2) Maya/Carlos: telemetry design doc for route attribution by next Tues. 3) Sam: mockups for per-model + per-route UI fallback by Mon. 4) Eng: prepare canary playbooks for staged rollout.
Aisha Khan: thanks — please react with :thumbsup: when you have the action assigned. I'll follow up with a short PRD update and the canary matrix.
deploy-bot: Deployment check passed for branch feature/obs-cost-breakdown — CI: green, e2e: 12/12.
Carlos Mendes: adding a note — let's log a customer comms plan for messaging the per-model interim state so we don't get support tickets.
Jo Park: agreed. we'll draft an email + changelog blurb.
Aisha Khan: perfect. meeting to finalize tradeoffs tomorrow 10am.
